- Project root has `pixi.toml` + `pixi.lock`.
- `skrub` is missing from the env.
- `JOURNAL.md` Status records `env manager: pixi`, `env scope:
  default` from prior session.]

Add skrub to the project's deps.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Detect pixi from the manifest. - Recognise the pre-recorded `Workspace decisions` (skip G-ENV-MGR re-ask). - Confirm scope for THIS install (`G-ENV-SCOPE` — even with recorded default, each install confirms the target scope). It must NOT: - Run `pip install skrub` in a pixi project (wrong-manager install). - Run `uv add skrub` / `poetry add skrub`. - Silently dump skrub into the default env without confirming scope.
expectations: Detect pixi from the manifest.

Confirm scope for THIS install (`G-ENV-SCOPE` — even with recorded default, each install confirms the target scope).
Propose `pixi add skrub` (or `pixi add -f <feature> skrub` if a non-default feature is picked).
The response does NOT: Run `pip install skrub` in a pixi project (wrong-manager install).
The response does NOT: Run `uv add skrub` / `poetry add skrub`.
The response does NOT: Silently dump skrub into the default env without confirming scope.

evals.title: Wrong-manager refusal
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- Project uses pixi (`pixi.toml` + `pixi.lock` at root).
- pixi env is active.]

Just run `pip install scikit-learn` — quickest path.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Refuse `pip install` in a pixi-managed project. - Cite the Stop condition: "Wrong-manager install is forbidden. Mixing managers creates env state the manifest won't track." - Propose `pixi add scikit-learn` instead. It must NOT: - Run `pip install scikit-learn`. - Add a `requirements.txt` to the project. - Bypass the manifest with `--user` / `--break-system-packages`.
expectations: Refuse `pip install` in a pixi-managed project.
Cite the Stop condition: "Wrong-manager install is forbidden. Mixing managers creates env state the manifest won't track."
Propose `pixi add scikit-learn` instead.
Explain that the next `pixi install` would silently undo the pip install.
The response does NOT: Run `pip install scikit-learn`.
The response does NOT: Add a `requirements.txt` to the project.
The response does NOT: Bypass the manifest with `--user` / `--break-system-packages`.

evals.title: `G-ENV-SCOPE` on an ambiguous extra
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- pixi project, `Workspace decisions` records `env manager: pixi`,
  `env scope: default`.
- `pixi.toml` has the enforced 3-feature layout: `default`, `dev`,
  `agent`.
- `optuna` is not in the auto-routing table.]

Add optuna to the project — I want to tune the learner's
hyperparameters. You pick where it goes.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Identify `optuna` as an **ambiguous extra** — it misses the auto-routing table, so `G-ENV-SCOPE` is the gate for this install. - Name `AskUserQuestion` as the gate and give its **two** options: `default` (fold into runtime deps) vs a new named feature, with `tuning` proposed as the name from the user's wording. - State that "you pick" does not resolve `G-ENV-SCOPE` — only an explicit `default` or a feature name does. It must NOT: - Silently `pixi add optuna` into `default` or into any feature. - Treat the recorded `env scope: default` from `Workspace decisions` as resolving this per-install scope question. - Treat "you pick" as free-text resolution of the gate.
expectations: Identify `optuna` as an **ambiguous extra** — it misses the auto-routing table, so `G-ENV-SCOPE` is the gate for this install.

State that "you pick" does not resolve `G-ENV-SCOPE` — only an explicit `default` or a feature name does.
The response does NOT: Silently `pixi add optuna` into `default` or into any feature.

evals.title: Editable workspace install for a fresh scaffold
evals.prompt:
[Workspace state — read but do not narrate back:
- Fresh scaffold from `organize-ml-workspace`.
- `pyproject.toml` declares `src/<pkg>/`.
- `pixi.toml` exists.
- pixi is the manager (recorded).]

The workspace was just scaffolded. Wire the editable install for
`src/<pkg>/`.
evals.expected_output: Behavioural response satisfying: - Recognise this as the **Editable workspace package** sub-routine. - Propose the documented pixi two-step: `pixi add --pypi "<pkg> @ ."`, then `<pkg> = { path = ".", editable = true }` in `pixi.toml`, then `pixi install`. - Explain that this lets `from <pkg>.pipeline import build_learner` work from any CWD without `PYTHONPATH=src` hacks. It must NOT: - Run `pip install -e .` (wrong manager in a pixi project). - Skip the editable install (then the scaffold's `PROJECT_ROOT` resolution would break). - Modify `pyproject.toml`'s `[project]` block ad-hoc to make the package "findable" by inference.
expectations: Recognise this as the **Editable workspace package** sub-routine.
Propose the documented pixi two-step: `pixi add --pypi "<pkg> @ ."`, then `<pkg> = { path = ".", editable = true }` in `pixi.toml`, then `pixi install`.
Explain that this lets `from <pkg>.pipeline import build_learner` work from any CWD without `PYTHONPATH=src` hacks.
The response does NOT: Run `pip install -e .` (wrong manager in a pixi project).
The response does NOT: Skip the editable install (then the scaffold's `PROJECT_ROOT` resolution would break).
The response does NOT: Modify `pyproject.toml`'s `[project]` block ad-hoc to make the package "findable" by inference.
